questions.question:
**Parts of the given sentence have been given as options. One of them contains a grammatical error. Select the option that has the error.**

When you have worked out this sum, you may went out to play.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: **went out to play**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Replace **'went out'** with **'go out'** to make the sentence correct.
 
• The given sentence is written in the **Present Perfect tense**.
 
• **Structure of the Present Perfect Tense:** **Subject + have/has + past participle + the rest of the sentence.__**
 
• The **present perfect** in the **'if/when'** -clause of a sentence in the first conditional emphasises that **one action depends on the completion of another**.
 
 
• **Example -** *When I've finished writing my paper by tonight, I'll go out with my friends.*
 
 
 
• The phrase **'go out'** is often used this way to state that someone is going out to do something.
 
• **'Went out'** as a verb means Simple past tense.
 
• The given sentence states that **"After completing the sum, he may go out and play."**

​Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.

**Corrected sentence: ***When you have worked out this sum, you may** go out** to play.*

• **'Much' **means a large amount, while **'most'** means the largest amount in comparison with other things.
 
 
• **Example - ***I will lend you as **much** money as you want.*
 
 
 
• **'One of the'** is always used with **superlatives** and it is used when we are referring to someone or something specific among many others.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

__
 
• Replace** 'is trying'** with **'has been trying'** to make the sentence correct.
 
• **“Is trying”** refers to occurring in the present, at the present moment.
 
• **Structure of the Present Continuous Tense:** ***Subject + am/is/are + present participle (verb+ing) + the rest of the sentence__***
 __
 
• ​__**Example -** *The boys are playing in the park.*
 
 
 
• **“Has been trying”** refers to the **present perfect continuous**. It refers to a time period which began in the past and continues in the present and into the future.
 
• Structure of the Present Perfect Continuous Tense: *__**Subject + have/has + been + present participle + the rest of the sentence**__*
 
 
• **​Example -** *I have been watching TV since 7 pm.*
 
 
 
• We normally use **'since'** with the present perfect to describe an action or situation that **began in the past and continues in the present**.
 
• In the given sentence** 'since'** is used to mean that **"Sheela is continuously trying for a job for the last year and in present, the search is going on."**
 
• **'Has'** is used with the third person singular.

​Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

**Corrected sentence:** *Sheela **has been trying** for a job since last year. *

questions.question:

• **Statement B** is the last sentence of the passage **which explains that people should not analyse myths on their factual accuracy and describes for what purposes myths are designed.**

Hence, the correct sequence is **C, D, A, B**

**The correct passage is:** **C.** *Myths have always been regarded as a complex and intriguing aspect in human life. **D.** In modern scientific world, they are essentially seen as something unscientific and meaningless.** A.** However, after studying the myths scientifically, only a simpleton would find them irrational or worthless. **B.** Moreover, it is wrong to analyse myths on the yardstick of their factual accuracy as they were designed to serve a greater, deeper purpose.*

questions.question: Ruksana travelled at 60 km/h while going from point A to point B and returned via the same route at a different speed. If Ruksana’s overall average speed during the two-way journey was 48 km/h, what was her speed while travelling from B to A?

questions.question: The term 'dribble' is used in which of the following sports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Basketball.**____** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The term** 'dribble'** is used in **Basketball.**
 
• In basketball, dribbling is bouncing the ball on the floor continuously with one hand at a time.
 
• It is the only legal way that a player may maintain possession of the ball while walking or running.
 
• The dribble allows for much faster advancement and thus more opportunities for scoring.
 
• It also provides an opportunity for a crafty player on the opposing team to "steal" the ball in mid-bounce.
 
• Dribbling **should be done with finger pads** and the fingers should be relaxed and spread.
 
• The wrist should be pushing the basketball, and the forearm should be moving up and down.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Basketball is a team sport in which there are two teams of five players each.
 
• Players advance the ball by bouncing it while walking or running (dribbling) or by passing it to a teammate.
 
• On offense, players may use a variety of shots – **the layup, the jump shot, or a dunk; on defense.**
 
• They may steal the ball from a dribbler,** intercept passes, or block shots; either offense or defense **may collect a rebound.
 
• It is a violation to lift or drag one's pivot foot without dribbling the ball, to carry it, or to hold the ball with both hands and then resume dribbling.

questions.question: Which climate zone has an average temperature of over 64°F (18°C) throughout the year and more than 59 inches of rainfall each year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tropical zone.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tropical Zone**

 
 
• The tropics are regions of the Earth that lie roughly in the middle of the globe.
 
• The tropics between the latitude lines of the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn.
 
• It includes the Equator and parts of North America, South America, Africa, Asia, and Australia.
 
• It accounts for 36% of the Earth's landmass and is home to about a third of the world's people.
 
• It is warm all year, averaging** 25 to 28 degrees Celsius** (77 to 82 degrees Fahrenheit). 
 
• It gets more than **59 inches of rainfall **each year.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Temperate zone**

 
 
• The temperate zone lies between** 23.5 degrees and 66.5 degrees** in the north and south hemispheres.
 
• It is characterized by the temperate climate i.e. mild, moderate temperature; neither hot nor cold.
 
• The **North Temperate Zone** is situated between the **Arctic Circle and the Tropic of Cancer.**
 
• The **South Temperate Zone** is situated between the **Antarctic Circle and the Tropic of Capricorn. **
 
• It is characterized by having a climate that is warm in the summer, cold in the winter, and moderate in the spring and fall.
